handoff.review_notes: Single-record batch. General (b*p-q)/b form from a live-inspected Stanford-hosted derivation (even-money f=q-p maximum, 5-to-1 f=(5q-p)/5 case, edge-over-odds rule) with two published worked oracles. No license statement on the source page; recorded honest-unknown.
handoff.summary: Kelly optimal wealth fraction for a simple win-or-lose bet from win probability and net odds.

assumptions: Source assumption: a simple bet that either pays net odds and returns the stake or forfeits the stake.
The criterion maximizes expected logarithmic wealth over repeated identical bets at known probability and odds.

gaps: New meanings kelly_net_odds and kelly_wealth_fraction (both dimensionless) need registry review; bernoulli_success_probability reuses existing vocabulary.

models.inverse_notes: p = (f*odds+1)/(odds+1) requires the result in [0,1]; the die case recovers (0.04*5+1)/6 = 0.2. odds = (1-p)/(p-f) requires p>f for positive odds; at p=f the odds are unidentified (any odds give the same zero edge). At p=1 the fraction is exactly 1 (bet everything on a sure thing); the source Sure Thing section agrees. No f>=0 guard is imposed: a zero or negative fraction is the valid no-bet signal, documented in limitations.
limitations: A zero or negative fraction means no edge: bet nothing rather than staking a negative amount.
Full Kelly assumes exactly known probabilities and repeatable bets; estimation error and ruin constraints favor fractional Kelly in practice.
Simultaneous or correlated bets need a portfolio treatment absent here.

relationship.locator: Biased Coin (f = q-p maximum), Loaded Dice (f = (5q-p)/5 with one-dollar expected profit 5q-p), Risk versus reward (bet edge/odds)
relationship.original_equation: f = edge/odds with edge = b*q-p (source notation); instantiated f=(5q-p)/5 for the die case and f=q-p for the even-money coin case
relationship.translation_notes: Source q (win probability) maps to p and source p (loss probability) to the introduced complement (1-p); net odds b maps to odds. The general (b*p-(1-p))/b is the source edge/odds rule with the die-case expected-profit form 5q-p generalized from b=5; the coin case f=q-p is the b=1 instance. Dimensionless throughout.

sources.evidence: Maximizing long-run log-wealth growth gives f=q-p at even money and f=(5q-p)/5 at 5-to-1; the general rule bets edge over odds where edge is expected profit per unit staked; worked fractions 0.2 (coin) and 0.04 (die).

models.summary: For a simple win-or-lose bet with win probability p and net odds b (profit per unit staked), the fraction of wealth maximizing long-run logarithmic growth is (b*p-(1-p))/b; zero or negative means no bet.
models.title: Kelly optimal wealth fraction for a simple bet
